Teacher's Note
This unit discusses the role of the government in providing public facilities as well as in implementing
laws that apply to market, factory and the working conditions of people. The aim is to allow
students to understand the ways in which this role of the government is linked to concerns addressed
in our Fundamental Rights. It is this link to rights that provides a connection to similar issues
raised in earlier chapters. Also the

activities.subject: Social
activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 7.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: The aim is to allow students to understand the ways in which this role of the government is linked to concerns addressed in our Fundamental Rights.
In the classroom discussion, it is crucial to separate the discussion on the importance of the government's role in providing public facilities from their current unequal provision.
This means that the fact that persons currently get different amounts of water should not be viewed as a reason for the government not being able to provide public facilities.
The Bhopal gas tragedy is discussed as an example of the lax enforcement of the laws.

activities.question: Write a short answer using key points from Chapter 7.
activities.instructions: Place the options in the correct placeholders. The sentence order must match the answer key.

correctItems.text: Shortage of water is one major reason why Siva can't bring his family to Chennai.
Padma works as a domestic help in Saidapet and lives in the nearby slum.
She pays a rent of Rs 650 for the hutment, which has neither a bathroom nor a tap connection.
For 30 such hutments there is a common tap at one corner, in which water comes from a borewell for 20 minutes twice daily.
